boundary: Documented predefined values and INTEGER variable/parameter range, with explicit prototype restrictions. Prior minimum-literal and storage assumptions are corrected. No controller observations or inferred MAXINT sentinel semantics.

rules.documented: ON/OFF are BOOLEAN with the same values as TRUE/FALSE. MAXINT is INTEGER +2147483647; MININT is INTEGER -2147483648. Predefined identifiers are recognized throughout the program.
rules.implemented: Four typed, case-insensitive scalar value expressions. Supported CONST/dimension/SELECT expressions and internal routines recognize them. Scalar arguments create independent temporaries using existing passing and numeric-conversion rules. Reports record physical use locations and definitions.
rules.restriction: Controller/motion/port/file predefined names remain unsupported. Redefinition, same-named fields/types/labels and aggregate/call contexts are blocked pending namespace evidence. These four names are not reclassified as KAREL reserved words.

rules.documented: MININT must be used in place of its numeric value -2147483648 in source.
rules.implemented: Bare/grouped unary-minus INTEGER literal forms for the minimum fail with E_MININT_LITERAL and a migration message. MININT is accepted, as are checked arithmetic results that equal the minimum. REAL literal forms retain separate existing representability rules.
rules.migration: Replace INTEGER source -2147483648 and -(2147483648) with MININT. Prior runtime minima remain valid INTEGER values; only source-literal spelling changes.
rules.tests: tests/test_predefined_constants.py: minimum literal negatives and MININT positives; existing range/parameter/overflow fixtures now use documented spelling

rules.documented: INTEGER variables and parameters range from -2147483648 through +2147483646, while MAXINT has the predefined value +2147483647.
rules.implemented: Signed 32-bit expression/constant values are retained. INTEGER checked storage/value-parameter writes reject MAXINT before modifying globals, locals, fields, elements or FOR counters. Checked INTEGER function results use the same conservative guard. References preserve previous destination values; prior writes elsewhere remain visible and routine frames unwind.
rules.restriction: The inspected documentation does not settle MAXINT special-state storage or function-return semantics. The prototype blocks those contexts rather than interpreting MAXINT as an uninitialized sentinel. This extends the documented variable/parameter restriction conservatively to checked function results.
rules.migration: Programs that stored numeric/expression/constant 2147483647 now raise a source-located runtime error. MAXINT remains usable in comparisons, constants and arithmetic whose eventual stored value fits the documented range.
rules.tests: tests/test_predefined_constants.py: IntegerStorageBoundaryTests, destination preservation and frame cleanup
